Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, Japan, Middle East, New Zealand, UK, Australia)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Middle East escalation (US airstrikes on Iran, Iranian retaliation) is driving oil prices higher, reigniting inflation concerns and pushing US 10-year yields to 4.812% — a high not seen since November 2023. The dollar is firming on safe-haven demand and rising rate hike expectations. Markets now price a 68% probability of a September Fed hike (up from ~40% a week prior), bolstered by Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks and Fed Governor Barr's hawkish commentary. Key near-term catalysts are Friday's jobs report (consensus: +56K) and August CPI, both due before the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. The yen remains under pressure above 160/USD despite BOJ rate hike expectations and a prior joint US-Japan intervention. NZD weakened despite a 25bp RBNZ hike, perceived as less hawkish than expected.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (YES — US yields, Fed rate hike expectations, and their ripple effects on global FX are the central thread throughout the article)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (85 — rate hike expectations are a dominant theme, reinforced by Warsh, Barr, and CME FedWatch pricing)
Probability of increase: 68% (as explicitly cited via CME FedWatch for September)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (10 — holding is implicitly the alternative scenario but receives no meaningful focus)
Probability of holding: 32% (residual from the 68% hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (0 — cuts are not mentioned or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (75 — decidedly hawkish: rising oil/inflation, 10-year yields at multi-month highs, hike probability jumping to 68%, and explicit hawkish signals from both Warsh and Barr; partially tempered by soft JOLTS and ISM data which have not materially shifted the overall trajectory)
